title: PCR or PLS?
description: Course activity for Exercise 9: compare how PCR and PLS construct a component differently when the target relates more strongly to a lower-variance predictor direction.
instructions: Choose a method (PCR or PLS), a number of components, and a preset that changes how strongly the target aligns with the predictors' lower-variance direction. The predictor cloud and the training/validation split stay fixed throughout; only the underlying target and the selected fit change.
reflectionPrompts: With one component, why can PLS outperform PCR?
Why do PCR and PLS become more similar after both original directions are retained?
Does a component that explains more predictor variance necessarily predict the target better?
Why would fitting PLS before the split be especially problematic?
